newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sees W. Canada wheat at 27.7 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: CWB sees W. Canada wheat at 27.7 mln tonnes.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board forecast above average yields in wheat and barley across western Canada, despite hot and dry conditions in August, a CWB weather analyst said during an industry briefing here Thursday.
The CWB estimated the western Canadian wheat crop at 27.7 million tonnes and barley at 14.9 million versus 23.85 million and 12.1 million, respectively in 1995.

"Hot, dry conditions in August caused some loss of that yield potential, but it was offset by the rapid crop maturation that maintained good grain quality," said CWB director of weather and crop survellience Paul Bullock.

The CWB's estimates were less than those issued by Statistics Canada, but greater than the 1995 crop. CWB had estimated 1995 wheat and barley production at 23.85 million tonnes and 12.1 million, respectively.
Based upon a July 31 crop survey, Statistics Canada had previously forecast 1996 western Canadian wheat production at 28.65 million tonnes and barely production at 15.27 million tonnes.
